prompt: An empty delivery van weighs $3{,}200$ pounds. It is loaded with boxes weighing $45$ pounds each, and it must cross a bridge with a weight limit of $5{,}000$ pounds. What is the maximum number of boxes the van can carry across the bridge?
hint: The bridge limit applies to the van and its load together. Think about how much of the limit the empty van already uses.

hints.text: The bridge limit applies to the van and its load together. Think about how much of the limit the empty van already uses.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try smaller numbers: a $10$-pound cart with a $25$-pound limit, carrying $5$-pound boxes. That leaves $15$ pounds, so $3$ boxes. Subtract the fixed weight, then divide by the per-item weight.
With $b$ boxes the weight is $3200 + 45b$, and it must satisfy $3200 + 45b \le 5000$. Subtract the weight of the van, then divide by $45$.
This gives $45b \le 1800$, so $b \le 40$. The van can carry at most $40$ boxes.

learningObjective: Solve a real-world capacity inequality with a whole-number answer.
explanation: The loaded weight is the van plus the boxes, $3200 + 45b$, and it must not exceed the limit: $3200 + 45b \le 5000$.
Subtract $3200$ from both sides to find the weight available for boxes: $45b \le 1800$.
Divide by $45$ to get $b \le 40$. The division is exact, so $40$ boxes bring the van exactly to the limit.
The maximum number of boxes is $40$.

alternativeExplanations.title: When to round down, and when not to
steps: If the division had come out to $40.7$, the answer would be $40$ — you cannot load a fraction of a box.
Here it divides evenly, and "$\le$" permits equality, so $40$ is achievable rather than one too many.
The rule: for a maximum with $\le$, take the floor of the quotient; an exact quotient is itself the answer.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: 5000 ÷ 45 ≈ 111 boxes ignores the truck itself — an answer both offered and absurd on reflection.
The van's 3,200 pounds use up capacity before the first box loads. Subtract the fixed weight, then divide.
